title: Ferromagnetic Phase Nucleation Kinetics in FeRh Mediated by Ultrafast Laser Pulses In-Situ in TEM
content: Obtaining a good understanding of nucleation processes during laser-induced magnetic phase transitions holds an immense significance to advance the integration of these materials in functional devices, such as sensors or memories [1]. FeRh, a binary alloy known for its unique metamagnetic phase transition from an antiferromagnetic (AF) to a ferromagnetic (FM) state near room temperature [see Fig. 1A], presents a rich platform for investigating nonequilibrium phase transitions [2-4]. FeRh has also been extensively studied for its coupled magnetic, structural, and electronic order parameters [5]. This interplay causes the magnetic phase transition to be accompanied by isotropic lattice expansion of its cubic lattice, reaching 0.3 % upon heating [6]. Consequently, FeRh offers broad possibilities in tuning the phase transition, among others, via applying strain [7].
